title: ANTILOCK BRAKE SYSTEM APPLICATIONS
content:
Copyright AA1Car
Every wonder what type of antilock brake system (ABS) is on your vehicle? Antilock brake systems have been around since the mid-1980s and have been supplied to vehicle manufacturers by various suppliers. These include Bendix, Bosch, Delphi (Delco), Kelsey-Hayes, Teves, and various Asian systems made under license from Bosch. Bosch bought Bendix several years ago, and the corporate ownership of Teves has changed several times.
Note: This ABS Application Guide chart was originally compiled in 1998, and was last updated in 2003, so it may not include the most recent applications.
For more information about each of these major ABS systems including an overview of how they work, diagnostic basics and fault codes, see ABS Guide.
ABS systems fall into several broad categories:
Integral systems: The master brake cylinder, ABS modulator and pump are integrated into one assembly. These were used on older vehicles but have been discontinued due to their high cost and service issues.
Nonintegral ABS: These are add-on ABS systems where the ABS modulator and pump are separate components from the master cylinder, and a conventional vacuum brake booster is ued.
Rear-wheel Only ABS: Used only on older trucks and SUVs. These have been replaced by four-wheel ABS systems on newer trucks and SUVs.
